rulings.grounds: Re-derived (skeleton tier, word-bound): the token intersection of oshb:Eccl.6.2 and oshb:Eccl.6.3 is non-empty -- 'ish' (man), 'mimmenu' (than-him/from-him), and 'lo' (to-him) all recur, 3 tokens. 'mimmenu' sits INSIDE the row's own byte-tier Hebrew quote at 6:3 ('tov mimmenu ha-nafel'), so the rejected_alternative denies a token the row itself is quoting -- OL's point, confirmed. Separately (LF's point, also confirmed against the tier-1 hevel_refrain inventory: 30 verses/38 tokens, oshb:Eccl.6.4 listed under the prefixed 'ba-hevel' form): 6.2 closes on bare hevel and 6.4 -- inside this row's own span -- opens with the prefixed hevel form, an undisclosed cross-seam echo of the book's own refrain. A nephesh-family (soul/appetite) echo also bridges 6.2/6.3/6.7/6.9 (re-derived by word-substring sweep: 7 verses book-wide, 4 in ch 6 -- correcting OL's own citation, which mislabels this a 'tier-1 device inventory' object; no nephesh entry exists in the device inventory, so it is a skeleton-tier self-sweep, not a tier-1 citation). LF and OL converge on the SAME underlying defect (the blanket 'no content token' denial); OL's evidence is the tighter of the two (an exact token inside the row's own quote), LF's is an independent second confirming instance.
rulings.remedy: Rewrite strongest_rejected_alternative to disclose the shared ish/mimmenu/lo tokens and the hevel/nephesh family echoes, then argue past them on the scenario-shift ground (new conditional clause, distinct case from the alien-eats-it scenario) rather than denying the tokens exist. Add a Hebrew splice for oshb:Eccl.6.2 wherever it is invoked for a content claim (engagement-class requirement -- the current field cites the reference but quotes no Hebrew from it). rulings.challenge_claim: The row's own closing verse, oshb:Eccl.6.9, is one of the 12 book-wide verse-initial tov-openers, undisclosed; the rejected_alternative never weighs a split at that signal.
rulings.grounds: Re-derived against the tier-1 tov_openers inventory (count_object: verses whose FIRST skeleton token is the tov/tova form; 12 book-wide: Eccl.4.6, 4.13, 5.4, 6.9, 7.1, 7.2, 7.3, 7.5, 7.8, 7.11, 7.18, 9.18) -- oshb:Eccl.6.9 is confirmed a member, and it is the only ch-6 member. device_notes discloses only the reut-ruach refrain at 6.9, not the tov-opener status. Both of the row's own seams are word-bound token-clean (6.6/6.7 and 6.9/6.10 intersections empty, independently re-confirmed), so the SPAN placement itself is not contested -- what is missing is disclosure of a real rival granularity signal at the row's own closing verse and its being weighed in rejected_alternative (which addresses only a 6.8-internal split). Chapter 6 sits in monologue_unit default territory (book strategy Section 6), not one of the two owner-ruled sentence zones (7:1-14, 9:17-10:20) where a verse-initial tov independently carries unit-opening force for a sibling row (e.g. web:Eccl.7.1) -- so the omission is a disclosure gap, not evidence that the boundary itself is wrong.
rulings.remedy: Add to device_notes that oshb:Eccl.6.9 is 1 of 12 book-wide (and the only ch-6) verse-initial tov-openers. Expand rejected_alternative to name and argue past a 'tov-opener could open its own unit' rival, distinguishing ch 6's monologue-default territory from the ch-7/ch-9 sentence zones where that convention operates under the owner's hybrid-atomic ruling. Test: any future universal or uniqueness claim about this verse must carry the tov-opener digit alongside the reut-ruach digit already cited.

rulings.challenge_claim: LF: the English gloss for oshb:Eccl.6.12 splices two separate WEB sentences into one quotation via an ellipsis, so quote and gloss do not share a span, leaving the verse's own hevel token and tachat-hashemesh close undisclosed. OL: the row's 'no shared vocabulary' claim for its opening seam is byte-false, and its closing seam is argued on a forbidden Tier-4 'chapter break.'
rulings.grounds: [Span mismatch, LF] WEB Eccl.6.12 clean text is two sentences ('...which he spends like a shadow? For who can tell a man what will be after him under the sun?'). The row's English gloss elides across both sentences via an ellipsis, while its Hebrew quote stops before the row's own suffixed hevel token ('hevlo', his vanity) and before the closing 'tachat ha-shamesh' (under the sun, 1 of 27 tachat-hashemesh sites) -- the Hebrew quote and the English gloss do not cover the same material; confirmed against verse_map_web.json and verse_map_oshb.json. [Disclosure + Tier-4, OL] Word-bound skeleton intersection of oshb:Eccl.6.7-6.9 and oshb:Eccl.6.10-6.12 is non-empty: 'tov' (6.9/6.12), 'hevel' (6.9/6.11), and 'yode'a' (knows; 6.8/6.12) -- 3 exact tokens, re-derived -- directly contradicting the row's 'no shared vocabulary' claim for its opening seam. The hevel_refrain tier-1 inventory (30 verses/38 tokens) lists both 6.9/6.11 (bare) and 6.12 (suffixed 'hevlo') -- a byte-true refrain straddles the row's own opening seam, undisclosed rather than argued past. Separately, boundary_rationale and rejected_alternative both cite 'a chapter break' for the closing seam; chapter/verse numbering is Tier-4 metadata and is NEVER boundary evidence under the standing rule -- a real (root-level, not word-bound-identical) name echo and an exact shared 'tov' token instead run from 6.12 into 7.1. LF and OL flag DISTINCT defects on the same row -- quote/gloss parity vs. rationale disclosure/forbidden-tier citation -- both independently confirmed, not duplicates.
rulings.remedy: (1) Re-cut the English gloss for 6:12 to match the Hebrew quote's own span (or extend the Hebrew quote to match the gloss's full range), and disclose the hevel-family and tachat-hashemesh tokens in device_notes. (2) Strike 'a chapter break' from boundary_rationale and rejected_alternative; replace with a content-argued closing warrant (e.g. the shift from meditative question to declarative tov-saying, argued from the bytes rather than from verse numbering). (3) Disclose the tov/hevel/yode'a cross-seam tokens at the opening edge and argue past them explicitly rather than asserting 'no shared vocabulary.' Test: quote/gloss parity check must pass (Hebrew and English quotations cover the same verse material); no Tier-4 term (chapter/verse break) may stand as sole or contributing boundary evidence in boundary_rationale or rejected_alternative.

rulings.challenge_claim: The row's sole named cohesion driver -- the 'house of mourning' phrase claimed to 'recur verbatim' and be 'byte-verified at both' oshb:Eccl.7.2 and oshb:Eccl.7.4 -- is tier-overclaimed; undisclosed tokens cross the closing seam and internal adjacency sits at the review-trigger threshold.
rulings.grounds: Re-collated at the byte-tier tool, using the exact phrase spliced from the row's own 7:2 citation: the phrase 'בֵּֽית אֵ֗בֶל' collates at BYTE tier against its source, oshb:Eccl.7.2, but only at SKELETON tier (contiguous-substring match, not exact) against oshb:Eccl.7.4, whose actual text carries a prefixed form, 'בְּבֵ֣ית אֵ֔בֶל' -- one extra letter (the prefixed preposition), a different word-bound token ('be-vet', not 'bet'). The row's own device_notes claim -- 'byte tier, byte-verified at both oshb:Eccl.7.2 and oshb:Eccl.7.4' -- and boundary_rationale's 'recurs verbatim' are both falsified at the tier they claim; the bracket survives only as a skeleton-tier (substring) echo -- real but weaker evidence than claimed. Closing-seam tokens: 'kesilim' (fools) is word-bound-identical across oshb:Eccl.7.4 and oshb:Eccl.7.5; a 'chakham'-family (wise) lexeme and a laughter-root family also bridge 7.4-7.6 (laughter root re-derived at exactly 2 ch-7 verses: 7.3 and 7.6) -- all undisclosed against the row's 'a different topic' framing for its closing seam. Internal cohesion: the word-bound content-token intersection of each adjacent pair inside the cluster is exactly 1 token (7.2/7.3 share only 'tov'; 7.3/7.4 share only 'lev', heart) -- at, not above, the owner-named saying_cluster review-trigger threshold (book strategy Section 7: cohesion thinner than 2 shared content tokens is an expected low-confidence flag).
rulings.remedy: Re-tier the device_notes cohesion-driver claim to 'skeleton tier (contiguous substring), not byte-identical at both ends' and disclose the exact 7:2/7:4 form difference (bare vs. prefixed). Disclose the kesilim/chakham-family/laughter-root cross-seam echoes at the closing edge and argue past them. Then either supply a stronger, correctly-tiered cohesion warrant that clears the named review-trigger threshold, or revert web:Eccl.7.2-7.4 to atomic single_saying rows under the sentence zone's hybrid-atomic default. The atomic split is a BOUNDARY CHANGE -- offered here as a candidate remedy only; adoption is the boss round's call, not authorized by this ruling. Test: the cited bracket phrase must re-collate to byte tier against BOTH cited verses before it may be called 'byte-verified at both' or 'verbatim'; if it does not, the driver must be relabeled to its true tier.

rulings.challenge_claim: The saying_cluster at web:Eccl.7.5-7.6 has ZERO shared word-bound content tokens between its two members; its sole driver (a verse-initial causal particle at 7.6) fails to discriminate against the very next verse, which opens with the same particle; and the row's 'sharing no vocabulary' claim about 7.7 is byte-false.
rulings.grounds: Word-bound skeleton intersection of oshb:Eccl.7.5 and oshb:Eccl.7.6 is empty, re-derived -- the thinnest possible case against the owner-named 2-shared-content-token review trigger for sentence-zone saying_cluster rows (book strategy Section 7). Verse-initial 'ki' (causal 'for/because') occurs at exactly 5 ch-7 verses -- 7.6, 7.7, 7.12, 7.20, 7.22, independently re-derived by checking every verse in the chapter -- including BOTH 7.6 (inside the cluster) and 7.7 (the verse the cluster is explicitly held apart from): the particle used to bind 7.6 backward into the cluster does not distinguish the seam it is asked to carry, since the immediately excluded neighbor opens with the identical particle. 'Chakham' (wise) is word-bound-identical across oshb:Eccl.7.5 and oshb:Eccl.7.7 -- re-derived: these are the ONLY two verses in the chapter carrying that bare form (checked 7:1-7:22) -- directly contradicting the row's rejected_alternative claim that 7.7 is 'an unrelated corruption saying, sharing no vocabulary.'
rulings.remedy: Either supply a genuinely discriminating byte-grounded cohesion driver for 7:5-7:6 that clears the named review-trigger threshold and does not also head the excluded neighbor verse, while disclosing and arguing past the chakham echo into 7:7; or revert web:Eccl.7.5 and web:Eccl.7.6 to atomic single_saying rows under the sentence zone's hybrid-atomic default. The split is a candidate boundary change only, pending boss-round adoption -- not authorized by this ruling. Test: the word-bound content-token intersection of the cluster's member verses must be non-empty and named in device_notes; any verse-initial-particle warrant must be checked against the immediately excluded neighbor's own first token before being cited as a discriminating boundary marker.

rulings.challenge_claim: LF: the row's claim that web:Eccl.7.7 'shares no content token with the fool's-laughter pair before it' is false ('chakham'/wise shared with 7.5). OL: additionally, the row's own quoted opening token for 7.7 IS the causal particle its rejected_alternative claims is absent from either neighbor, and an undisclosed heart-token chain links 7.7 backward into the mourning bracket.
rulings.grounds: Both items fully confirmed at word-bound/skeleton tier. (1) 'Chakham' (wise) is the identical skeleton token at oshb:Eccl.7.5 and oshb:Eccl.7.7 -- LF's finding, independently reconfirmed. (2) OL's addition: the row's own boundary_rationale Hebrew quote for 7.7 opens with the causal particle 'ki', and oshb:Eccl.7.6 -- the preceding neighbor the rejected_alternative describes as lacking 'a repeated phrase or causal particle linking it to either neighbor' -- ALSO opens with 'ki' (confirmed: verse-initial 'ki' occurs at exactly 5 ch-7 verses including this adjacent pair). The row denies, in its own rejected_alternative, a particle its own quoted text supplies. (3) A heart-root ('lev') token chain runs oshb:Eccl.7.2 (suffixed 'libo'), 7.3, 7.4 (bare 'lev'), and 7.7 (bare 'lev') -- re-derived, 4 ch-7 verses -- an undisclosed backward link into the 7.2-7.4 mourning bracket the mesh closes at 7.4. LF's own severity call (low, reasoning the atomic verdict is 'still defensible') undersells the finding once OL's self-contradiction and heart-chain points are added: the row's rejected_alternative is affirmatively wrong on two separate fronts (a token it shares and a particle it quotes), not merely incomplete on one. The forward boundary (7.7/7.8) IS word-bound token-clean, independently confirmed, and remains the row's real basis for keeping 7:7 atomic.
rulings.remedy: Rewrite rejected_alternative for 7:7 to: (a) stop denying the chakham echo with 7.5 and instead argue past it (corruption/bribery topic vs. hearing-preference topic remain genuinely distinct even though the lexeme recurs); (b) stop claiming an absent causal particle when the row's own quote opens with one -- ground the atomic verdict instead in the genuinely clean forward boundary (7.7/7.8, token-empty intersection, confirmed); (c) disclose the heart-token chain into the mourning bracket. Test: rejected_alternative may not assert the absence of a lexical feature (particle or token) that appears in the row's own cited quote or its immediate neighbor's cited quote.

rulings.challenge_claim: LF and OL independently flag the same two defects at web:Eccl.7.8: the tov-opener count blends a verse-object digit with a clause-object digit ('5th and 6th of 7' for one verse), and the row discloses the Tier-4 WEB paragraph fold into 7.9 while leaving a real Tier-1 ruach/spirit echo into the same verse undisclosed.
rulings.grounds: The tier-1 tov_openers inventory (count_object: verses whose FIRST skeleton token is tov/tova; 12 book-wide) contains oshb:Eccl.7.8 exactly ONCE, as the 5th of the chapter's 7 members (7.1, 7.2, 7.3, 7.5, 7.8, 7.11, 7.18) -- re-derived and confirmed. The verse's second 'tov' clause (token index 4, not verse-initial) cannot be a second opener occurrence under that count_object's own definition, so 'the 5th and 6th of 7' double-counts one verse-object as two against a 7-member list that still contains 7.11 and 7.18 undrawn. Separately: oshb:Eccl.7.8 carries the 'ruach' (spirit) root twice (bare), and oshb:Eccl.7.9 opens with the same root in a prefixed+suffixed form -- re-derived, and this is the ONLY other ruach occurrence anywhere in ch 7 (every verse 7:1-7:22 checked) -- the row's own most-repeated token recurs in the immediately following verse, undisclosed, while the Tier-4 WEB paragraph fold across the same seam IS disclosed (a disclosure-priority inversion: Tier-4 formatting disclosed, Tier-1 lexical recurrence withheld). LF and OL independently found the identical pair of defects -- true convergence, not complementary distinct findings.
rulings.remedy: Correct device_notes to 'oshb:Eccl.7.8, 5th of the chapter's 7 tov-opener sites (one verse, two internal tov clauses -- only the verse-initial one counts under the opener's own count_object)'. Add disclosure of the ruach/spirit root recurring into oshb:Eccl.7.9 alongside the existing (correct) Tier-4 fold disclosure. Test: any digit citing the tov-opener inventory must match a verse-count, not a clause-count, against the 12-member list; the seam-adjacent device disclosure at a verse must cover Tier-1 lexical signals with at least the same completeness as any Tier-4 formatting note made about the same seam.
